subject: Throughput acceptance criteria — post-call snapshot and next steps
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liu <emma@cartiq.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 13:04:00 -0700
Subject: Throughput acceptance criteria — post-call snapshot and next steps

Hi Emma — thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap from our side and a small set of follow-ups so we can size the Dedicated pilot and draft acceptance criteria.

Key points we captured on the call:
- Target latency SLOs: 95th <= 250ms for short inference responses; 99th <= 500ms for end-to-end streaming completion (customer-visible).
- Steady-state: ~40 QPS across API endpoints, average request = ~600 tokens (generation + context) => rough steady tokens/sec = 24k.
- Peak microbursts: up to 420 QPS for 3–5 minute windows, with some requests spiking to 1.2k–1.5k tokens.
- Concurrency: expected 120 concurrent long-poll streaming sessions during peak; streaming sessions typically emit first token within 100–150ms and then steady-rate deltas.
- Region: primary traffic originates in us-east (Virginia); DR and fallback traffic will come from us-west occasionally.

Open clarifying asks (can you confirm the bullets below?):
1) Can you confirm average tokens per request and % requests that hit >1k tokens (we heard ~12% on the call).
2) For streaming sessions: are clients using chunked streaming (server pushes tokens as generated) or polling? Also any websocket keepalive/settings we should know about.
3) Expected business impact window for the 3–5 minute bursts — are these hourly events, or triggered by specific user journeys?
4) Any hard constraints on cold-start latency for model switchovers or can we accept a short degraded window during failover?

Next steps we propose from Redwood:
- If you can send a 24–72 hour sample of request-level telemetry (csv preferred) and one representative streaming trace, we will produce a pilot sizing proposal (number of GPUs, expected tail latency under load, cache suggestions).
- Draft acceptance criteria doc (SLOs + burst handling) and a proposed rollback/fallback model for canary failures.
- Follow-up sync: 30m next Thu to review sizing and contract milestone alignment.

I attached a small template (cartiq_workload_sample.csv) for the telemetry export — if your team can populate the columns we highlighted in the template it will speed the sizing pass.

Thanks —
Michael Grant
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: cartiq_workload_sample.csv (text/csv)
From: Emma Liu <emma@cartiq.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@cartiq.com
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 14:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput acceptance criteria — post-call snapshot and next steps

Thanks Michael — appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers inline.

1) Average tokens per request: 620 tokens. Roughly 10–15% of requests exceed 1k tokens (these are longer summary requests).
2) Streaming: clients use chunked server-sent-events (SSE) — we do not use websockets today. Typical cadence is first token ~120ms, then ~1 token per 80–120ms thereafter for active stream. Keepalives are sent every 30s.
3) Burst windows: primarily triggered by scheduled digest generation (every hour on the hour) plus occasional marketing-driven campaigns that create multi-hour elevated load. The microbursts are most commonly the hourly digests (3–7 minutes).
4) Cold-start: procurement/legal wants model-switch latency to be under 2 minutes for traffic migrations; for pilot we can accept a brief degraded window but they will require a documented fallback plan.

I’ve attached a 48-hour telemetry extract and one sample latency trace (client_latency_trace_20270517.json). Procurement looped in in case we move to a PO stage.

Best,
Emma Liu
Head of Platform Engineering | CartiQ Solutions
emma@cartiq.com | +1 (212) 555-3344

Attachment: client_latency_trace_20270517.json (application/json)
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liu <emma@cartiq.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput acceptance criteria — post-call snapshot and next steps

Emma — thanks for the fast turnaround and the telemetry. We pulled the sample and started an initial quick pass. High-level next steps from Redwood Ops + Solutions: 

- We will run a 2-phase pilot sizing: (1) a scaled soak to validate steady-state and concurrency at 40 QPS / 120 concurrent streams, and (2) an engineered microburst test to emulate the 420 QPS 3–5 minute window with realistic token-size mix.
- Deliverables: pilot sizing report (incl. GPU count, instance types, expected 95/99 tail latencies), acceptance criteria draft, and a short runbook for failover + canary policies.
- Data asks: please also export a sample network pcap or aggregated egress-bandwidth numbers for a 1-hour peak; that will help sizing for connection multiplexing and NIC requirements. (We noticed some spikes in the trace that could be client-side batching.)
- Proposed follow-up: Thu May 20, 10:00am ET (30m) to review pilot proposal and procurement asks. 

I attached a small network trace bundle request note (network-trace.zip) as a checklist — if procurement prefers our SOW language up front we can send a short PO-ready statement of work.

Michael/Markus — I’ll take point on the pilot sizing; Markus can own the microburst engineering run. Emma — sending calendar invite now.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai

Attachment: network-trace.zip (application/zip)
